4e0caa1a76.q: What is the story of the 62-62 vote tie in the Mississippi House Speaker election?
4e0caa1a76.a: Edward Blackman Jr. was running to be elected temporary Speaker of the House, a test vote for the full Speaker election. Billy McCoy was running for Speakership against Republican candidate Robert Johnson. There was a 62-62 vote tie twice. Edward's own seatmate of 14 years initially voted for Robert Johnson, but after Barbara convinced Representative Tyrone Ellis to change her vote, Edward Blackman Jr. won on the third call and became temporary Speaker of the Mississippi House of Representatives. This was described as monumental and the first time in Mississippi history since Reconstruction that a Black person achieved this role.

ddecfe54a7.q: What does Barbara Blackmon identify as the biggest misunderstanding about division in America today?
ddecfe54a7.a: Barbara Blackmon says the biggest misunderstanding is a lack of education, knowledge, and communication. She emphasizes that if you have values and purpose—a purpose-driven life—you would not freely abdicate your own thoughts and power by just regurgitating what someone else has said. Instead, you must learn and study information for yourself rather than blindly following soundbites, and you should read multiple sources like the New York Times, the Post, the Hill, and local newspapers to develop your own discernment.

85ce26c800.q: What percentage of American adults read at least one book per year as of recent data cited in Two Minds, One Rhythm?
85ce26c800.a: Barbara Blackmon cited that in 2010, 55% of adults read at least one book a year, but this has dropped to 49%. She also noted that universities and colleges are struggling with how to encourage their students to read, highlighting the decline in reading habits as a significant concern for informed citizenship.

15773e2f4d.q: What is the secret to Barbara and Edward Blackmon's long marriage according to the book Two Minds, One Rhythm?
15773e2f4d.a: Barbara Blackmon says the secret to their marriage is communication, separation, and building family. In their law practice they maintain separate sides of the building; in the legislature he was on the House side and she was on the Senate side. When they left work and the legislature, it was 100% family time. The secret is balancing separateness, togetherness, and prioritizing family time, a model they observed in Edward's parents.

d1214a4771.q: How did Molly Blackman, Edward Blackman Jr.'s mother, help her children succeed despite segregation and hardship in Mississippi?
d1214a4771.a: Molly Blackman's own mother died when she was three years old and her father also died, but her aunt Ophelia helped her get education at a time when Black women could not go past sixth or seventh grade. Later, Molly taught her own children at home when they were forced to attend school only half-days during cotton-picking season in Canton, Mississippi, while white children attended all day. She obtained encyclopedias and Edward read them two to three times, building the knowledge that helped him finish Tougaloo College in three and a half years and George Washington University Law School in two and a half years.
